data.long_meaning: In Hebrew mythology, Samael is considered the Angel of Death. In Christian tradition, he is associated with the devil or Satan, representing darkness and evil. The name Samael carries the meaning “God of the dusk” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Samael usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the dusk and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the struggle between good and evil.
data.etymology: Samael belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the dusk.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Samael total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Σαμαήλ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Σαμαήλ σημαίνει ακροατής του Θεού ή φύλαξ του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σαμαήλ είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'ακροατής του Θεού' ή 'φύλαξ του Θεού'. Στην παράδοση των Χριστιανών, ο Σαμαήλ θεωρείται ως ένας από τους αρχάγγελους ή ως πνευματικό ον που λειτουργεί ως μεσολαβός μεταξύ του Θεού και των ανθρώπων.

in_latin.name: Samael
in_latin.meaning: Samael means listener of God or guardian of God
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Samael is derived from Hebrew roots and is interpreted as 'listener of God' or 'guardian of God'. In Christian tradition, Samael is sometimes regarded as an angel or spiritual being who acts as a mediator between God and humanity, tasked with guarding or listening to divine commands.

in_english.name: Samael
in_english.meaning: Listener of God or Guardian of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Samael originates from Hebrew, combining 'shem' (name or meaning) and 'El' (God). It translates to 'listener of God' or 'guardian of God'. Samael appears in biblical contexts as an angelic being, often associated with roles of protection or divine communication. In Christian tradition, Samael is viewed as a significant spiritual figure, embodying vigilance and obedience to God's will.

data.cultural_impact: Samael, derived from the Hebrew word "Showmel" meaning "God of the Blinding Anger," is a figure in Jewish and Christian mythology. In Jewish texts, he is considered a fallen angel responsible for the initial sin leading to humanity's expulsion from Eden. In Christian tradition, Samael has become synonymous with Satan or the devil. His name has evolved to signify temptation, darkness, and evil forces. In popular culture, many entertainments explore the intrigue of Samael as the embodiment of evil.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, Samael represents the struggle between good and evil. His existence signifies the hardships and temptations that humans may face in their quest for morality and adherence to God. Samael symbolizes the challenge that exists within each individual to choose between the path of righteousness and the path of destruction. In Christianity, Samael embodies the temptation Satan presents to humanity, serving as a reminder of the importance of resisting evil and staying true to one's faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Samael, often personified as the "Angel of Death" in Jewish folklore, symbolizes the relentless cycle of life and death, reminding us of our mortal nature and the impermanence of worldly existence. His name, meaning "venom of God," underscores the bitter-sweet truth that even in the face of death, there is a divine will at work.

biblical_reference.note: In apocryphal texts like 1 Enoch, Samael is mentioned as a significant angelic being.

historical_references.reference: In Jewish mythology, Samael is identified as the Angel of Death, the embodiment of sin, and the accuser of mankind before God. This role is similar to the Christian Satan, but Samael is not usually considered as an adversary to God, but rather as an enforcer of God's will.

In Christian demonology, Samael is described as a fallen angel, the serpent in the Garden of Eden, and the devil who tempted Adam and Eve. This portrayal is closer to the more adversarial role of Satan in Christianity.

modern_usage.modern_context: Samael, traditionally known as the 'Angel of Death' in Jewish folklore, has gained significant popularity in modern culture. He is commonly featured in various forms of media, particularly in tabletop role-playing games, horror fiction, and anime/manga. In these contexts, Samael is often depicted as a powerful, enigmatic figure who shapeshifts between good and evil, or is even a force of chaos. The exact nature of his role varies from work to work, but his presence adds intrigue and complexity to the story.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Samael, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Samael meaning "God of the dusk" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
